newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Brent edges up, small rebound seen.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Brent edges up, small rebound seen.

text.p: Brent crude futures in Asia were slightly firmer in late afternoon dealings on Tuesday, supported by a technical rebound, brokers said.
They said there was little direction for the market and they expected mostly sideways trading in the next few days.
However, Brent could rebound to $22.70 on March, after the slide in prices late last week, before finding resistance. Support was pegged at $22.35, Monday's intraday low in London.
March Brent on SIMEX was last traded at $22.57 per barrel, up three cents from London, which on Monday edged up just two cents as traders searched for direction.
NYMEX crude matched the generally steady nature of the market. March was last traded at $24.23 per barrel on ACCESS, up eight cents from the New York close.

March heating oil on ACCESS was also rebounding after losing ground in recent sessions on weather forecasts that temperatures in the key U.S. northeast would be normal in coming days and not lower than normal as had been previously forecast.
March was last traded at 65.55 cents per gallon, up 0.27 cent from New York where it had fallen 0.88 overnight.
